items.text: HYDROLYSISOFATERTIARYHALOGENOALKANE

items.label: text
items.text: The equation for the alkaline hydrolysis of 2-chloromethylpropane is:

items.label: formula
items.text: (CH₃)₃CCl + OH⁻ → (CH₃)₃COH + Cl⁻

items.label: text
items.text: The experimentally determined rate equation for this reaction is: rate =k[(CH)CCl]

items.label: text
items.text: The reaction is first order with respect to 2-chloromethylpropane, butzeroorderwithrespecttothehydroxideion.

items.label: text
items.text: Thesensibleconclusiontoreachisthatthe2-chloromethylpropane undergoes slow ionisation as therate-determining step.This is then followed by a very fast step involving attack by the hydroxide ion on thecarbocationformed inStep1.

items.label: formula
items.text:
Step 1: (CH₃)₃CCl → (CH₃)₃C⁺ + Cl⁻  SLOW
Step 2: (CH₃)₃C⁺ + OH⁻ → (CH₃)₃COH  FAST

items.label: formula
items.text: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Cl + OH⁻ → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH + Cl⁻

items.label: text
items.text: This type of mechanism is named Sn1,i.e.Substitution Nucleophilic unimolecular.

items.label: text
items.text: The rate-determining step is said to be unimolecular because there is only one reactant particle present, (CHs)sCCl.

items.label: text
items.text: The carbocation, (CHs)C+, formed in Step 1 is an intermediate (seeSection 11A.6).
